sizecheck.content.h1: What Is Image File Size and Why Does It Matter?
sizecheck.content.p1a: Image file size measures the total volume of digital storage space consumed by a graphic file, expressed in bytes, kilobytes (KB), or megabytes (MB). Whether you manage an e-commerce catalog, run a WordPress blog, optimize landing pages for SEO, or attach photos to an email, knowing the precise file size of your images is essential for fast performance and reliable delivery.
sizecheck.content.p1b: Oversized images are the leading cause of slow page loading times, poor mobile user experiences, and downgraded Google Search rankings under Core Web Vitals. Using ImgFeel's Image File Size Checker, you can instantly inspect exact byte counts, decimal and binary unit conversions, bits-per-pixel compression efficiency, and estimated network transfer speeds without uploading any files to external servers.

sizecheck.content.h2: Units of Image File Size: Decimal (KB) vs. Binary (KiB)
sizecheck.content.p2a: In digital computing, storage units are calculated using two distinct standards: the decimal metric system (SI) based on powers of 10 (1000) and the binary system (IEC) based on powers of 2 (1024). Web browsers, cloud storage providers, and network APIs generally use decimal KB (1,000 Bytes) and MB (1,000,000 Bytes).
sizecheck.content.p2b: Conversely, operating system file managers like Windows Explorer historically compute file sizes using binary kibibytes (1 KiB = 1,024 Bytes) and mebibytes (1 MiB = 1,048,576 Bytes) while still labeling them as KB or MB. sizecheck.content.h3: File Size vs. Pixel Dimensions vs. Image Resolution
sizecheck.content.p3a: A common point of confusion is equating pixel dimensions with file size. Pixel dimensions describe the geometric grid width and height (e.g. 1920 × 1080 px = 2.07 Megapixels). File size describes how many bytes of data are needed to store those pixels on disk.
sizecheck.content.p3b: Two images with identical 1920 × 1080 pixel dimensions can have radically different file sizes. An uncompressed 24-bit bitmap PNG with intricate textures might weigh 4.5 MB, while the exact same visual compressed into modern WebP format at 80% quality might weigh only 120 KB — a 97% reduction with virtually imperceptible visual difference.

sizecheck.content.h7: How Image File Size Impacts Core Web Vitals & Page Speed
sizecheck.content.p7a: Google uses Core Web Vitals as an official ranking factor in search results. Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures how quickly the main content of a page (frequently a hero image or banner) finishes rendering. An oversized 3 MB hero image on a mobile 4G connection can delay LCP by several seconds, resulting in poor search rankings and high bounce rates.
sizecheck.content.p7b: Compressing images to under 200 KB and converting legacy formats to WebP or AVIF directly optimizes First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Time to Interactive (TTI), delivering near-instant page experiences across all mobile devices.

sizecheck.faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
sizecheck.faq.q1: How do I check the file size of an image online for free?
sizecheck.faq.a1: Drag and drop your image into the ImgFeel box above or select a file. You can also paste directly from your clipboard with Ctrl+V. The tool instantly calculates exact bytes, KB, MB, compression density, and network download speeds.
sizecheck.faq.q2: Are my images uploaded to any server during analysis?
sizecheck.faq.a2: No. All file size calculations and binary inspections run 100% locally in your web browser. Your images never leave your computer or phone.
sizecheck.faq.q3: What is the difference between KB and KiB?
sizecheck.faq.a3: A Kilobyte (KB) uses the decimal system and equals 1,000 bytes. A Kibibyte (KiB) uses the binary system and equals 1,024 bytes. Operating systems like Windows use binary KiB, while web networks use decimal KB.
sizecheck.faq.q4: What is considered a good image file size for a website?
sizecheck.faq.a4: For standard blog and content images, 70 KB to 150 KB is ideal. For large fullscreen hero banners, keep files under 300 KB. Icons and logos should be under 25 KB.
sizecheck.faq.q5: How can I reduce the file size of an image that is too large?
sizecheck.faq.a5: You can reduce file size by compressing it with modern WebP compression, lowering the quality to 80-85%, or resizing the pixel dimensions to match the actual display container size.
sizecheck.faq.q6: What is Bits Per Pixel (BPP) and how does it measure compression?
sizecheck.faq.a6: Bits Per Pixel (BPP) divides total file bits by total image pixels. Lower BPP values (e.g. 0.3–1.0 bpp) indicate highly efficient compression, while values above 3.0 bpp suggest the file is uncompressed or overly heavy.
sizecheck.faq.q7: Can I check the file size of WebP, AVIF, SVG, and GIF files?
sizecheck.faq.a7: Yes! ImgFeel supports all raster and vector image formats including JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, SVG, GIF, BMP, ICO, and TIFF.
